help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The tickets are checked at the entrance.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: An action in progress uses werden + Partizip II; ist gewaschen would describe the finished state.
help.tips[0].en.text: Das Auto | wird | gerade | repariert. Die Briefe | werden | jeden Tag | gebracht. Question: Wird das Auto repariert? Negation: Das Auto wird nicht repariert.
help.tips[0].en.title: werden + Partizip II at the end
help.tips[0].en.trap: the English passive uses 'be' (is repaired); the German action passive uses werden. 'Das Auto ist repariert' is a state (it's done); 'wird repariert' is the action (being done).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: They're building a house here. → A house is being built here.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The mechanic is repairing the car. → The car is being repaired.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The accusative object den Salat becomes the nominative subject der Salat, wird stays in position 2 and the participle goes last.
help.tips[1].en.text: Der Mechaniker repariert das Auto. → Das Auto wird (vom Mechaniker) repariert. The accusative object moves to the front and becomes nominative; the old subject goes into von + dative or disappears.
help.tips[1].en.title: Active → passive: the object becomes the subject
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The letter is written by the secretary.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The guests are greeted by the boss in person.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: The person doing the action follows von + dative; durch and für would need the accusative.
help.tips[2].en.text: Die Rechnung wird von meinem Chef bezahlt (by whom). Die Stadt wurde durch ein Erdbeben zerstört (by what means). Most passives name no doer at all — that is their point.
help.tips[2].en.title: von + dative for the doer; durch for the means
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: People drink a lot of beer in Bavaria. → A lot of beer is drunk in Bavaria.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: People separate rubbish in Germany. → In Germany rubbish is separated.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: A man-sentence turns into a passive with werden; with no subject left, it takes the singular wird.
help.tips[3].en.text: Every 'man' sentence is a passive in waiting: Man spricht hier Deutsch = Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen. Man öffnet das Geschäft um neun = Das Geschäft wird um neun geöffnet. If you can say it with man, you can say it in the passive.
help.tips[3].en.title: man ↔ passive
help.context.en: In our bakery work starts every morning at four. The dough is made by two bakers, the rolls are baked at six. The shop is opened at seven, and by noon almost everything is sold. What's left is delivered to the food bank. And in the evening everything is cleaned – by me.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: werden agrees with the plural subject.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The doer takes von + dative, and the participle is last.
help.hookEn: Say how things get done without naming who does them, just like signs, recipes and news reports: Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen.
help.introEn: The present passive, met earlier for recognition, is now yours to build: werden in position 2, the Partizip II at the end, and the doer — if named at all — after von + dative. Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen. Das Auto wird gerade repariert. Die Briefe werden jeden Tag gebracht. Die Rechnung wird von meinem Chef bezahlt. The passive is chosen when the action matters more than the actor (rules, processes, notices, recipes, news), and it is the normal voice of instructions and descriptions of how things are done — which makes it a core reading structure and a useful writing one (In unserer Firma wird viel Englisch gesprochen). werden agrees with the new subject — the thing the action is done to: Das Brot wird gebacken; die Brötchen werden gebacken. In the quiz you type both halves: the form of werden, which agrees with the new subject (wird / werden), and the Partizip II at the end.
help.rememberEn[0]: wird / werden at 2, participle last; the thing done-to is the subject.
help.rememberEn[1]: von + Dat = by whom; no doer is the normal case.
help.recallEn.known: From "Passiv Präsens: Das wird gemacht": werden + participle.
help.recallEn.today: Turning an active sentence round, and von for the doer, durch for the means.
sentences[0].whyEn: Passive: werden + participle at the end; plural Sprachen → werden … gesprochen.
sentences[1].whyEn: Singular: wird … repariert — -ieren takes no ge-.
sentences[2].whyEn: Plural: werden … gebracht — bringen's mixed-verb participle.
sentences[5].whyEn: wird … abgeholt — the prefix wraps the ge-.
sentences[8].whyEn: wird … bezahlt — von names the doer.
sentences[13].whyEn: wird … getrennt — the famous waste-sorting, as a passive.
sentences[14].whyEn: werden … begrüßt — be- takes no ge-.
sentences[15].whyEn: Subjectless passive: wird … gearbeitet — 'no working here'.
